source_text:
Homilia de jejunio (homilia 15) (e cod. Sinaitico gr. 491)
Ησυχίου, πρεσβυτέρου Ἱεροσολύμων, περὶ νηστείας.
1 Ῥίζα καὶ θεμέλιος τῶν εὐσεβῶν ἡ κατὰ θεὸν νηστεία, ἡ μετὰ εὐλαβείας καὶ
ἁγίων εὐχῶν καὶ ἐλεημοσυνῶν ἐπιτελουμένη. Οὐ γὰρ ἀποχὴν ἄρτου καὶ ὕδατος
βούλεται ὁ θεός, ἀλλ' ἀποχὴν πράξεων πονηρῶν· «Οὐ γὰρ τὰ εἰσερχόμενα εἰς τὸ
στόμα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλὰ τὰ ἐκπορευόμενα ἐκ τοῦ στόματος, ἐκεῖνα κοινοῖ
τὸν ἄνθρωπον.» Νηστεύσωμεν, ἀγαπητοί, νηστείαν τὴν θεῷ πρέπουσαν, περὶ ἧς
φησιν ὁ κύριος· «Σὺ δὲ ὅταν νηστεύῃς, ἄλειψόν σου τὴν κεφαλὴν» δι<ὰ> καλῶν
ἔργων καὶ ἐλεημοσυ νῶν, «καὶ τὸ πρόσωπόν <σου> νίψαι», περιαιρῶν πᾶσαν
ῥυπαρίαν ἁμαρτίας. Ἔστιν νηστεία ψεκτὴ καὶ ἔστιν νηστεία ἐπαινετή. Πολλοὶ
νηστεύσαντες φόνους εἰργάσαντο καὶ πολλοὶ νηστεύσαντες ἄλλους ἔσωσαν.
2 Ἐνήστευσαν Νινευῖται καὶ ἐσώθησαν καὶ διὰ τῆς νηστείας τὸν θυμὸν τοῦ
θεοῦ μετέβαλον. Καὶ ἀπόφασιν ἐξενεχθεῖσαν κατ' αὐτῶν ἡ νηστεία ἐκώλυσεν· φησὶν
γὰρ ὁ προφήτης· «Ἔτι τρεῖς ἡμέραι καὶ Νινευὴ καταστραφήσεται.» Οὐκ εἶπεν «μετὰ
τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ Νινευὴ καταστραφήσεται»· εἰ γὰρ εἶπεν «μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας»,
κατεστράφη ἄν, ἀλλ' «ἔτι τρεῖς ἡμέραι», τοῦτο δεικνὺς ὅτι «Τοσοῦτον χρόνον
ἠνειχόμην ὑμῶν καὶ οὐ μετενοήσατε. Ἔτι τριῶν ἡμερῶν ἀνέχομαι ὑμῶν καί, εἰ μὴ
ἐν ταῖς τρισὶν ἡμέραις μετανοεῖτε, ἔπειτα καταστραφήσεται ἡ πόλις.» Καὶ τοσοῦτον
χρόνον οὐ μετενόησαν, εἰ μὴ διὰ τῶν τριῶν ἡμερῶν τουτέστιν διὰ τοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ
Υἱοῦ καὶ ἁγίου Πνεύματος.
3 Ἐνήστευσαν Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ συμβούλιον ἔλαβον ἵνα τὸν ἀπόστολον Παῦλον
ἀποκτείνωσιν. Ἐκήρυξεν Ἰεζάβελ νηστείαν καὶ τὸν Ναβουθαὶ ἀπέκτεινεν καὶ τὸν
ἀμπελῶνα τοῦ πένητος ἔλαβεν. Νηστεία καὶ φόνος αὕτη ποία νηστεία; Ἐνήστευσεν
∆ανιὴλ ὅτε ἐβλήθη εἰς τὸν λάκκον τῶν λεόντων· βληθέντος γὰρ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν
λάκκον, ἐβό<α> πρὸς Χριστὸν λέγων· «Ἐκ βαθ<έων> ἐκέ<κραξά σε, κύριε·> κύριε,
εἰσάκουσον τῆς προσευχῆς μου.» Βλέπων δὲ τοὺς λέοντας ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ ἐξ
εὐωνύμων, πάλιν ἐβόα λέγων· «Μὴ παραδῷς τοῖς θηρίοις ψυχὴν ἐξομολογουμένην
σοι.» Βλέπε δὲ ὅτι οὐκ ἐγκαταλιμπάνει κύ ριος τοὺς ἐλπίζοντας ἐπ' αὐτόν. Ὁ μὲν
βασιλεὺς ὁ ἐπίγειος ἐ σφράγισεν τὸν λάκκον, ὁ δὲ ἐπουράνιος βασιλεὺς ἐσφράγισεν
thought_title: Fasting as root of piety, and its two kinds
orientation: Hesychius, a presbyter of Jerusalem, opens his homily by defining true fasting as abstinence from evil deeds, not merely from bread and water, and then begins contrasting a blameworthy fast with a praiseworthy fast through biblical examples.
pass_a_gloss: Of Hesychius, presbyter of Jerusalem, concerning fasting. Root and foundation of the pious is the fasting according to God, the one accomplished with reverence and holy prayers and almsgivings. For God does not wish abstinence from bread and water, but abstinence from evil deeds: "For not the things entering into the mouth defile the man, but the things coming out of the mouth, those defile the man." Let us fast, beloved, a fasting befitting God, concerning which the Lord says: "But you, whenever you fast, anoint your head" through good works and almsgivings, "and wash your face", removing every filth of sin. There is a blameworthy fast and there is a praiseworthy fast. Many having fasted committed murders and many having fasted saved others. The Ninevites fasted and were saved and through the fasting changed the wrath of God. And the sentence brought out against them the fasting prevented; for the prophet says: "Yet three days and Nineveh will be overthrown." He did not say "after three days and Nineveh will be overthrown"; for if he had said "after three days", it would have been overthrown, but "yet three days", showing this, that "So much time I bore with you and you did not repent. Yet for three days I bear with you and, if you do not repent in the three days, then the city will be overthrown." And so much time they did not repent, except through the three days, that is through the Father and Son and Holy Spirit. The Jews fasted and took counsel that they might kill the apostle Paul. Jezebel proclaimed a fast and killed Naboth and took the vineyard of the poor man. Fasting and murder, this what kind of fasting? Daniel fasted when he was thrown into the den of the lions; for when he was thrown into the den, he cried out to Christ, saying: "Out of the depths I cried to you, Lord; Lord, hear my prayer." And seeing the lions on the right and on the left, again he cried out, saying: "Do not hand over to the beasts a soul that confesses to you." And see that the Lord does not abandon those who hope in him. The earthly king sealed the den, but the heavenly king sealed

choices.why: Keeps the prepositional force of κατὰ θεὸν, which marks the fast as conforming to God's will, not merely 'godly' as an adjective.
ἀποχή is a noun of abstaining; rendering it as 'abstinence' preserves the parallel structure with 'abstinence from evil deeds' in the next clause.
Uses the fixed glossary rendering for this key term, which the homily contrasts with the praiseworthy fast.
Uses the fixed glossary rendering for this key term, the positive counterpart to the blameworthy fast.
Uses the fixed glossary rendering for ἐλεημοσύνη, keeping the plural to match the source.
The verb βοάω means to cry out or shout; 'cried out' preserves the intensity and the direct address to Christ.

pass_b_english: Fasting according to God is the root and foundation of the pious, when it is carried out with reverence, holy prayers, and almsgiving. For God does not desire abstinence from bread and water, but abstinence from evil deeds. “For it is not what enters the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of the mouth—that defiles a person” (Matthew 15:11). Let us fast, beloved, a fast that befits God, about which the Lord says: “But you, when you fast, anoint your head” with good works and almsgiving, “and wash your face,” removing every stain of sin. There is a blameworthy fast, and there is a praiseworthy fast. Many who fasted committed murders, and many who fasted saved others.

The Ninevites fasted and were saved, and through fasting they changed the wrath of God. And fasting blocked the sentence that had been pronounced against them. For the prophet says: “Yet three days, and Nineveh will be overthrown” (Jonah 3:4). He did not say, “After three days, Nineveh will be overthrown.” For if he had said, “After three days,” it would have been overthrown. But he said, “Yet three days,” showing this: “For so long I bore with you, and you did not repent. Yet for three days I bear with you, and if you do not repent within the three days, then the city will be overthrown.” And for so long they did not repent, except through the three days—that is, through the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.

The Jews fasted and took counsel to kill the apostle Paul. Jezebel proclaimed a fast and killed Naboth and took the poor man's vineyard. A fast and murder—what kind of fast is that? Daniel fasted when he was thrown into the lions' den. For when he was thrown into the den, he cried out to Christ, saying: “Out of the depths I have cried to you, O Lord; Lord, hear my prayer” (Psalm 129:1-2 [130:1-2]). And seeing the lions on his right and on his left, again he cried out, saying: “Do not hand over to the beasts a soul that confesses you” (Psalm 73:19 [74:19]). See that the Lord does not abandon those who hope in him. The earthly king sealed the den, but the heavenly King sealed

These are restored in the gloss according to the editorial brackets.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'of the pious ones' (people); English 'the pious' reads as abstract adjective, losing the personal sense.
last_rejected.ruling: 'The pious' is standard English for 'pious ones/people'; personal sense intact.

last_rejected.source_quote: Ἐκ βαθ<έων> ἐκέ<κραξά σε, κύριε·> κύριε, εἰσάκουσον τῆς προσευχῆς μου

last_rejected.ruling: Notation '129 (LXX) = 130 (Hebrew)' is standard; brackets correctly show Hebrew equivalent. Not wrong.
